info.description:
Zeus is the execution plane for faults-lab. Manteion issues
commands to it. This document is the integration contract between
the two. Run lifecycle state machine and cross-cutting concerns
(dataset handshake, error envelope) are documented in
docs/api-contract.md.
info.title: Zeus Load Generation API

get.description:
Returns a bare array of attacks. Optional query filters narrow by status,
experiment_id, and run_ref.

parameters.description: filter by attack status (e.g. running, completed)
parameters.name: status

post.description:
Persist and launch a precision attack. The body is an attacker.AttackConfig.
When run_ref references an existing run, meta_trace_id and workflow_label are
inherited from the linked run if not set on the request. The response is an
inline envelope with id, status, and started_at; the launched Attack object is
retrievable via GET /attacks/{id}.

202.description: attack accepted; envelope contains id, status, started_at

400.description: invalid JSON or attack validation error

delete.description: Cancels a running attack and decrements the active-attacks gauge.

get.description:
Returns an inline envelope with attack_id, status, config, optional result
(vegeta-derived totals + latency percentiles), and optional dedup strategy
metadata when DedupBypass is configured on the attack.

200.description: attack stats envelope (attack_id, status, config, result?, dedup?)

post.description:
Persist a dataset shell. Source is one of "upload" (NDJSON push), "inline"
(synthesized by run-create from dataset_inline), or "cache_box_dump" (future).
Defaults: source="upload", ttl_s=86400 (24 h). Rows are pushed separately via
POST /datasets/{id}/upload.

201.description: envelope: id, name, source, created_at, ttl_s

delete.description: Refuses with 409 when an active run still references the dataset.

409.description: dataset is in use by an active run

get.description:
Returns an envelope with id, name, source, pool_stats (per-pool row_count,
size_bytes, fields), size_bytes, ttl_s, created_at. Use GET /datasets/{id}/sample
to inspect rows.

Returns up to limit rows (default 10, capped at 100) from the named pool.
The response envelope is { "pool": "<name>", "rows": [...] }.

post.description:
Streams NDJSON pool batches into the dataset. Each line is
{"pool":"<name>","rows":[{...},...]}. The endpoint is lenient: per-line decode
errors are collected and returned in the response body but do not abort the
ingest. The response envelope contains ingested (per-pool counts), total
(rows accepted), and an optional errors array.

400.description: ingest error (e.g. dataset not found at ingest time)

get.description:
Returns 200 with {status: ok} once the process accepts requests. Dual-mounted
at root (/healthz) and /api/v1/healthz; the @Router uses the bare path key
so spec consumers composing servers[0].url + path resolve correctly.

Returns a stats.Summary with active_runs, active_attacks, datasets, and
uptime_seconds. Companion to GET /metrics (Prometheus scrape) for callers
that don't speak Prometheus.

Returns 200 with {status: ready} when the metric registry and in-memory stores
are initialized. Dual-mounted at root (/readyz) and /api/v1/readyz.

Returns an envelope { "runs": [...] }. Filters are AND-combined; "since" must be
RFC 3339 (invalid timestamps are silently ignored).

delete.description:
Transitions a non-terminal run to "stopped". Refuses with 409 when the run is
already in a terminal state (completed/stopped/failed/rejected). On success,
Prometheus per-run label series are pruned and SSE subscribers are closed.

409.description: run is already in terminal state

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream of run lifecycle and per-step events. Event types
emitted: step.ok, step.drop, iteration.done, phase.transition. Used by manteion
for live dashboards; not the canonical aggregated stats source. The Last-Event-ID
header is reserved for future resumable-stream support; the current handler does
not parse it (subscriber starts at the live edge).

parameters.description: Last event ID for resumable stream (reserved; not yet honored)
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

500.description: streaming not supported by the underlying response writer

get.description:
Returns the finalized RunStats snapshot for a run. While the run is still in
flight (or finished without a snapshot persisted), responds 200 with a minimal
envelope { "run_id": ..., "status": "no stats available yet" } instead of 404.
The handler is tagged "metrics" rather than "runs" because it serves aggregate
numbers, not run-document state.

Returns active_runs, active_attacks, datasets, and uptime_seconds plus a
status string. Computed from live store counts on every call.

Returns an envelope { "workflows": [...] } where each entry is a compact
summary (id, name, version, targets) — not the full DSL document. Use GET
/workflows/{id} for the full document.

post.description:
Persist a Zeus DSL v2 workflow. The body envelope wraps the workflow object
alongside an overwrite flag; when overwrite is true, an existing workflow with
the same name is replaced. Schema validation runs before persistence; failures
return 400 with the validator error string. Name conflicts without overwrite
yield 409.

400.description: invalid JSON or workflow validation error

delete.description:
Refuses with 409 when any non-terminal run is still bound to the workflow;
callers should stop those runs first.

get.description:
Returns an envelope { "runs": [...] } of all runs (including terminal) bound
to the workflow.

post.description:
Starts a run for the given workflow. Either dataset_id or dataset_inline (capped
at 1 MiB) may be supplied — they are mutually exclusive. When the workflow
declares a DataSchema, the dataset is validated; failures produce a terminal
"rejected" run and a 422 response with {run_id, status, reason}. Other run-level
rejections (workflow not found, run_id conflict, oversized inline) return their
natural codes; the run is not persisted in those cases. The success body is a
202-Accepted envelope of run_id, status, meta_trace_id, k6_job_name, started_at.

400.description: invalid JSON, mutually exclusive dataset fields, or pool shape error

404.description: workflow or referenced dataset not found

422.description: dataset failed schema validation; run created in rejected state

post.description:
Runs ValidateDataset against the workflow's DataSchema. Workflows without a
DataSchema short-circuit to {ok: true, warnings: []}. The result body is a
dataset.ValidationResult. Returns 422 (not 400) when the dataset fails schema
validation, mirroring run-create's rejected semantics. 400 is reserved for
malformed request bodies.
